1.meaning: A conditional/temporal particle meaning 'when' or 'whenever' — it sets up a circumstance and points forward to the event that will happen once that circumstance arrives. Here it introduces the great cosmic events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle of time and condition, so it has no case ending that changes. It governs the verb that follows and means roughly 'at the moment when…'; it normally refers to something certain or expected to occur, unlike 'in' (if) which marks the merely hypothetical.

2.meaning: The sky, the heaven — the vast canopy above, including the celestial expanse that will be torn apart on the Day of Judgment.
2.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' (ḍamma) is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject — the one performing/undergoing the action of the following verb ('the sky' is what splits). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the 's' (a 'sun letter'), which is why it is pronounced 'as-samā'u'.
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness, that which is above

3.meaning: It split open, was rent asunder, cleaved apart — the sky tearing and breaking apart violently.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form VII (the 'in-' pattern), which carries a passive/reflexive sense — the action happening to the subject of itself ('became split'). The suffix '-at' marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she did'), agreeing with the feminine noun 'sky'. Past tense here describes a future certainty as if already accomplished.
3.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave, tear apart

1.meaning: And it gave ear, listened attentively, and so submitted in obedience — the idea is hearkening to a command and yielding to it. The sky 'listens' to its Lord and complies without resistance.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form I, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The verb 'adhina' literally means 'to lend an ear,' here implying ready obedience. The suffix '-at' marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it listened'), agreeing with the feminine 'sky'.
1.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — the ear; hearing, giving heed, granting permission

2.meaning: To/for its Lord — 'Lord' (Rabb) means the Master, Sustainer, Owner and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs His creation. The pronoun 'its' refers back to the sky.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') attached to the noun 'Rabb', followed by the attached possessive pronoun '-hā' ('its'). The '-i' ending on 'Rabb' is genitive, required because it follows the preposition 'li-'; it shows the sky listened and submitted *to* its Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and ownership

3.meaning: And it was made duty-bound, rightly obligated — it was its proper duty and right that it should obey. The sense is that compliance was fitting and incumbent upon it.

parts.en: it was made an obligation / it was right (passive verb stem)

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) PASSIVE verb in Form I, shown by the 'u-a' vowel pattern ('ḥuqqa' = 'it was made obligatory'), prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The '-at' suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it was…'), agreeing with the feminine 'sky'. The passive leaves the One who obligates (Allah) understood.
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and rightly obligatory

1.meaning: And when — joining a second condition to the first; it introduces another event of the Last Day ('and when the earth…').
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to the indeclinable time-and-condition particle 'idhā' ('when'). 'Idhā' has no changing case ending; it governs the verb that follows and points to an event expected to occur.

2.meaning: The earth — the ground, the land, this terrestrial world that will be levelled and stretched flat.
2.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' (ḍamma) is the nominative ending, marking it as the grammatical subject of the following verb. Because that verb ('was spread out') is passive, 'the earth' is the substitute subject (nā'ib al-fāʿil): it takes the nominative as the verb's subject, even though it is the thing the action is done to. The 'l' of 'al-' is pronounced clearly here because 'a' (alif/hamza) is a 'moon letter'.

3.meaning: It was stretched out, drawn flat, extended and levelled — the earth being pulled and spread into a wide, even expanse (its mountains flattened away).

parts.en: it was stretched/spread out (passive verb stem)

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) PASSIVE verb in Form I, shown by the 'u-a' vowel pattern ('mudda' = 'it was extended'), with the doubled 'd' from the geminate root. The '-at' suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it was…'), agreeing with the feminine 'earth'. The passive leaves the One who spreads it (Allah) understood.
3.root: م-د-د (m-d-d) — to extend, stretch, draw out, prolong

1.meaning: And it cast out, threw forth, flung up and away — the earth expelling whatever lies within it (the dead and its buried contents) onto its surface.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV (the causative 'a-' pattern: 'to throw/cast out'), prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The '-at' suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it cast out'), agreeing with the feminine 'earth'. Form IV here gives the sense of actively flinging something forth.
1.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, throw, cast, put forth

2.meaning: A relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it stands for an unspecified thing or things; here, 'what is in it,' i.e. all the contents the earth holds within.
2.grammar: An indeclinable relative pronoun ('that which'), with no changing case ending. Grammatically it serves as the object of the verb 'cast out' — it is *what* the earth ejects — and it introduces the following phrase that describes it ('…that which is in it').

3.meaning: In it / within it / inside it — locating the contents inside the earth. The pronoun 'it' refers back to the earth.
3.grammar: The preposition 'fī' ('in/within') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it'). Together with the preceding 'mā', it means 'that which is *in it*' — describing the buried contents the earth holds and then throws out. Pronouns attached to prepositions take this object form; '-hā' here points back to the feminine 'earth'.

4.meaning: And it (the earth) emptied itself out, becoming utterly void — having cast out whatever was within it (its dead, its treasures), it is left vacant and clear.

parts.en: it emptied itself / became void (past tense)

4.grammar: A past-tense verb of the reflexive 'tafa''ala' pattern, which carries the sense of a thing doing something to/for itself — here the earth voiding itself. The final '-at' is the suffix for a feminine singular subject in the past tense, i.e. 'she/it (the earth) did it'; the earth (al-ard) is grammatically feminine. The reflexive form stresses that the emptying was thorough and complete.
4.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty, vacant, devoid

1.meaning: And it gave ear, listened attentively, and so submitted in obedience — the idea is hearkening to a command and yielding to it. The sky 'listens' to its Lord and complies without resistance.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form I, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The verb 'adhina' literally means 'to lend an ear,' here implying ready obedience. The suffix '-at' marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it listened'), agreeing with the feminine 'sky'.
1.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — the ear; hearing, giving heed, granting permission

2.meaning: To/for its Lord — 'Lord' (Rabb) means the Master, Sustainer, Owner and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs His creation. The pronoun 'its' refers back to the sky.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') attached to the noun 'Rabb', followed by the attached possessive pronoun '-hā' ('its'). The '-i' ending on 'Rabb' is genitive, required because it follows the preposition 'li-'; it shows the sky listened and submitted *to* its Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and ownership

3.meaning: And it was made duty-bound, rightly obligated — it was its proper duty and right that it should obey. The sense is that compliance was fitting and incumbent upon it.

parts.en: it was made an obligation / it was right (passive verb stem)

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) PASSIVE verb in Form I, shown by the 'u-a' vowel pattern ('ḥuqqa' = 'it was made obligatory'), prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The '-at' suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it was…'), agreeing with the feminine 'sky'. The passive leaves the One who obligates (Allah) understood.
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and rightly obligatory

1.meaning: A compound call meaning 'O…!' used to address and summon someone with emphasis. It is the standard Qur'anic way of calling out before an important announcement; here it grabs the listener's full attention.

parts.en: particle of attention reinforcing the call

1.grammar: This is a vocative (calling) construction: 'yā' is the particle 'O', and 'ayyuhā' is a special connecting word used when calling a noun that carries 'al-' (the). It does not inflect for case here in the usual way; its job is purely to summon. The attached 'hā' is an extra attention-drawing element. Together they prepare the listener for the noun being addressed ('humanity', which follows).

2.meaning: The human being; humankind — the species 'man' considered collectively. As the one being called, it denotes every person, the whole of humanity addressed by their Lord.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the human being') used here in a generic sense for the whole species. The final '-u' is the nominative (subject) ending; it marks this word as the one being addressed/named in the call — it is the noun summoned by the preceding 'O…'. The 'al-' generalizes it to mankind as a whole rather than one specific person.
2.root: أ-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar, human

3.meaning: 'Indeed you…' — an emphatic opener asserting something about 'you' with certainty. The particle 'inna' stresses the truth of the statement that follows, removing any doubt, and 'you' is its subject.
3.grammar: 'Inna' is an emphasis particle meaning 'indeed/truly' that introduces a noun sentence and grammatically governs the noun after it (putting it in the accusative). Here that noun is the attached pronoun '-ka' ('you', masculine singular), which serves as the subject of the emphatic statement. The whole word asserts with certainty: 'Truly, you…'.

4.meaning: One who toils, strives, and labours hard — a person exerting painstaking effort. It pictures the human being struggling laboriously through life on the way to meeting his Lord.
4.grammar: An active participle ('one who is doing X') of the form 'fāʿil', describing the doer of the action — here a toiler/striver. The final '-un' (nunation) is the indefinite nominative ending, meaning 'a labourer' and marking it as the predicate that completes 'you are…': 'you are one who toils'.
4.root: ك-د-ح (k-d-ḥ) — to toil, strive, exert oneself strenuously

5.meaning: 'To / toward' — a preposition marking the goal, end-point, or direction of motion. Here it points to the destination of the human being's striving: toward his Lord.
5.grammar: An indeclinable preposition meaning 'to/towards/up to', expressing the end-limit or goal of an action. It has no case ending of its own; instead it puts the following noun into the genitive case (here 'rabbika', 'your Lord'). It frames the toil of the previous word as directed toward a goal.

6.meaning: Your Lord — your Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs you. 'Rabb' conveys far more than 'lord': the One who brings a thing up stage by stage and cares for all its needs.
6.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with the attached possessive pronoun '-ka' ('your', masculine singular), so 'your Lord'. The '-i' ending is genitive, here because the word follows the preposition 'ilā' ('to'): 'toward your Lord'. The attached 'your' both possesses the noun and is itself in the genitive as a possessor.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, bring up

7.meaning: Strenuous toil; hard, painstaking exertion. It is the act of labouring itself, named as a thing — the wearisome effort the human pours out on the road to his Lord.
7.grammar: A verbal noun (the action named as a noun: 'toiling'). The final '-an' (nunation) is the indefinite accusative ending; here it functions as an emphasizing object that reinforces the participle 'kādiḥun' before it — literally 'toiling a toiling', i.e. 'labouring with real exertion'. It stresses how strenuous the effort is.
7.root: ك-د-ح (k-d-ḥ) — to toil, strive, exert oneself strenuously

8.meaning: 'And so you will meet Him' — i.e. you are bound to encounter your Lord (and the outcome of your toil). It conveys the certain, inevitable meeting with Allah at the end of one's striving.
8.grammar: 'Fa' is a connector meaning 'and so/then', linking this as the result of the toil. 'Mulāqī' is an active participle ('one who meets') of the 'mufāʿil' pattern, used here with future force ('you will meet'). It is a defective (weak-final) participle: in the indefinite nominative it would be 'mulāqin' (مُلَاقٍ, with the final yāʾ suppressed), but here it joins the pronoun '-hi' ('Him') as its object, forming a construct (iḍāfa). In that construct the nunation drops and the stem yāʾ is restored as the long '-ī'; that '-ī' marks the construct state, not a specific case ending. So: 'and so (you are) one who will meet Him'.
8.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come face to face

1.meaning: 'Then as for…' — a phrase that opens a new section and singles out one group or case for comment ('now, regarding…'). It sets up a contrast about to be drawn between two kinds of people.
1.grammar: 'Fa' is a connecting particle ('then/so'), and 'ammā' is a detailing particle meaning 'as for…', used to introduce and isolate one case for separate treatment. Neither takes a case ending. The construction typically pairs with a later 'fa-' that begins the answer ('…then he…'), and here it begins the description of one category of people.

2.meaning: 'Whoever / the one who' — a relative word standing for an unspecified person or persons defined by what they do. Here it means 'the one(s) who' are given their record, introducing the group being described.
2.grammar: A relative/conditional pronoun referring to a person ('the one who, whoever'). It is indeclinable, with no case ending, and is built on a silent (sukūn) ending. It functions here as the subject singled out by 'as for…', and is then explained by the verb that follows ('…is given his record'). Though singular in form, it can carry a collective sense ('those who').

3.meaning: 'He was given / is given' — he received something handed to him by another (here, his record). The passive form leaves the giver unnamed but understood, focusing on the person who is handed the book.

parts.en: passive stem vowel + final root letter yāʾ

3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb of the Form IV 'afʿala' (causative 'to give/bring to') pattern, in its passive shape 'ufʿila': 'he was given'. Being passive, the doer (the giver) is unstated, and the focus is on the receiver. The three root letters are hamza–tāʾ–yāʾ; the final yāʾ here is a ROOT consonant, not part of the ending. The only personal suffix is the final fatḥa (ـَ), which marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'): 'he was given…'. The long 'ū' at the start is not a stray root letter but a regular feature of the pattern: the passive prefix vowel 'u-' combines with the weak initial radical so that 'uʾti-/uwti-' is realized as 'ūti-'.
3.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative, Form IV) to bring/give

4.meaning: His record or written account — specifically the book/scroll in which all of a person's deeds have been recorded, here referring to the individual's personal scroll of deeds handed to them on the Day of Judgment.
4.grammar: A masculine noun carrying an attached possessive pronoun 'his'. The -a vowel on the stem (kitāba-) is the accusative ending, marking it as the direct object — 'the one who is given his record'. The attached -hu ('his') refers back to the person; it appears as -hu (with u) here because the preceding vowel is the accusative 'a'.

5.meaning: In his right hand — receiving the record of deeds in the right hand is the sign of salvation and a good outcome on the Day of Judgment. 'Yamīn' means the right side or right hand, traditionally the side of blessing and good fortune.
5.grammar: The prefix bi- ('in/with') is a preposition that always forces what follows into the genitive case — hence the -i ending on yamīni-. The attached -hi ('his') likewise takes the i-form because it follows the genitive vowel i. Together: 'in his right hand'.
5.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — the right side; by extension good fortune, blessing

1.meaning: Then soon / then in due course — a connective 'then' joined to a particle that points to the future, signalling that what follows is going to happen. It conveys near-certain futurity, often with a reassuring sense of 'it will surely come to pass'.
1.grammar: Fa- is a connecting particle ('then/so') that links this clause to what came before. Sawfa is a future-tense particle placed before a present-tense verb to push its meaning into the future — like English 'will' or 'shall', with a nuance of 'in time, soon'. Neither piece takes a case ending; particles are indeclinable (their form never changes).

2.meaning: He will be called to account / his reckoning will be carried out — the act of having one's deeds reviewed and audited by Allah. The verb form here is passive: the person is the one being held to account, not the one doing the accounting.

parts.en: be held to account (Form III passive stem)

2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he is/will be held to account'. It breaks into the prefix yu- and the Form III stem ḥāsab- (built on the root ح-س-ب, whose three radicals are ḥ-s-b). The yu- prefix together with the internal vowel pattern (yu-ḥā-sa-bu) marks the passive — the subject undergoes the action rather than performing it. The final short vowel -u on the stem is the indicative mood ending (the default mood for a plain statement); it is just a vowel on the last radical b, not a separate suffix. With sawfa before it, the sense is future: 'he will be called to account'.
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — counting, reckoning, calculating an account

3.meaning: A reckoning / an accounting — the process of having one's deeds counted, weighed and audited. Here it is the inner object of the verb 'to be reckoned with', emphasizing the reckoning itself before it is described as 'easy'.
3.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of reckoning) in the accusative case, shown by the -an ending (the nunation 'an' also makes it indefinite, 'a reckoning'). It functions as a cognate object reinforcing the verb yuḥāsabu — literally 'he will be reckoned a reckoning' — a common Arabic device for emphasis. The -an ending is what marks both the accusative case and the indefiniteness.
3.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — counting, reckoning, calculating an account

4.meaning: Easy / lenient / untroubled — describing the reckoning as light and gentle. For the believer the audit of deeds is made effortless and forgiving, in contrast to the harsh, prolonged reckoning of others.
4.grammar: An adjective in the accusative case (-an ending), matching the noun it describes, ḥisāban ('a reckoning'), which is also accusative and indefinite — 'an easy reckoning'. Arabic adjectives agree with their noun in case, number and definiteness, so the -an here mirrors the -an on ḥisāban. (The doubled y- at the start, yy-, is an assimilation to the preceding word in recitation.)
4.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — ease, facility, being made easy

1.meaning: And he will turn back / return — to go back and return to one's family. The verb's form carries a sense of turning around completely and going home, here joyfully returning to one's loved ones after the reckoning.

parts.en: he (3rd-person present prefix) + form VII reflexive marker

1.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he turns back / returns'. The n- built into yan-qalib- is the marker of a reflexive verb pattern (form VII), giving the sense 'to turn oneself around, return'. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for stating a fact. Prefixed wa- means 'and', linking it to the previous statement; (its w is doubled, ww-, by assimilation to the preceding word).
1.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — turning, overturning, the heart; here turning back / returning

2.meaning: To / towards — a preposition indicating the end-point or direction of a movement; here marking the goal 'to' which the person returns (his family).
2.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/towards'. Like all prepositions it is indeclinable (its own form never changes) and it puts the following noun into the genitive case. Its job is purely to link the verb 'return' to its destination — 'return TO his people'.

3.meaning: His family / his people — one's household and kinfolk, the close relatives to whom one belongs. In context, the saved person returns rejoicing to his family (understood by many to include his family in Paradise).
3.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive 'his'. It is in the genitive case (-i ending on ahli-) because it follows the preposition ilā ('to'), which always governs the genitive. The attached pronoun -hi ('his') takes its i-form here because it follows that genitive i vowel. Together: 'to his family'.
3.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, household, belonging, being inhabited

4.meaning: Joyful / delighted / happy — in a state of gladness and rejoicing. It describes the person as filled with happiness as he returns to his family, the fruit of a good reckoning.
4.grammar: A passive participle ('one who has been gladdened, made joyful') in the accusative case, shown by the -an ending. It is accusative because it describes the state or condition of the subject of 'he returns' — a 'circumstantial' description telling us HOW he returns: 'he returns joyful'. This kind of state-describing word in Arabic regularly takes the accusative -an ending.
4.root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r) — joy, happiness, gladness; delight of the heart

1.meaning: But as for… — a two-part connector introducing a contrasting case. 'And' joins to a particle meaning 'as for / regarding', which sets up a new subject for special comment, typically contrasting it with what was said before (here, contrasting the wretched with the saved).
1.grammar: Two indeclinable particles. Wa- ('and/but') links to the preceding passage. Ammā is a topic-introducing particle meaning 'as for…', used to single out a subject and signal that a comment (usually a contrast) is coming — it normally pairs with a later fa- ('then') in the answering clause. Neither particle takes a case ending.

2.meaning: 'Whoever / the one who' — a relative word standing for an unspecified person or persons defined by what they do. Here it means 'the one(s) who' are given their record, introducing the group being described.
2.grammar: A relative/conditional pronoun referring to a person ('the one who, whoever'). It is indeclinable, with no case ending, and is built on a silent (sukūn) ending. It functions here as the subject singled out by 'as for…', and is then explained by the verb that follows ('…is given his record'). Though singular in form, it can carry a collective sense ('those who').

3.meaning: 'He was given / is given' — he received something handed to him by another (here, his record). The passive form leaves the giver unnamed but understood, focusing on the person who is handed the book.

parts.en: passive stem vowel + final root letter yāʾ

3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb of the Form IV 'afʿala' (causative 'to give/bring to') pattern, in its passive shape 'ufʿila': 'he was given'. Being passive, the doer (the giver) is unstated, and the focus is on the receiver. The three root letters are hamza–tāʾ–yāʾ; the final yāʾ here is a ROOT consonant, not part of the ending. The only personal suffix is the final fatḥa (ـَ), which marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'): 'he was given…'. The long 'ū' at the start is not a stray root letter but a regular feature of the pattern: the passive prefix vowel 'u-' combines with the weak initial radical so that 'uʾti-/uwti-' is realized as 'ūti-'.
3.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative, Form IV) to bring/give

4.meaning: His record or written account — specifically the book/scroll in which all of a person's deeds have been recorded, here referring to the individual's personal scroll of deeds handed to them on the Day of Judgment.
4.grammar: A masculine noun carrying an attached possessive pronoun 'his'. The -a vowel on the stem (kitāba-) is the accusative ending, marking it as the direct object — 'the one who is given his record'. The attached -hu ('his') refers back to the person; it appears as -hu (with u) here because the preceding vowel is the accusative 'a'.

5.meaning: Behind / beyond — the area at one's back. Here it describes the record of deeds being given from behind the back (a sign of disgrace and a bad outcome, in contrast to receiving it in the right hand).

parts.en: behind / beyond / at the back of

5.grammar: An adverb of place ('behind') that functions like a preposition: it is in the accusative form (the final -a vowel, warāʾa) as such place-words regularly are, and it governs the following noun in the genitive — 'behind his back'. It tells us the location from which the record is handed over.
5.root: و-ر-ي / و-ر-ء (w-r-ʾ) — being behind, the rear, what lies beyond

6.meaning: His back — i.e. the back of the body. In context (84:10) the record is given 'from behind their backs,' an image of disgrace, the left hand being twisted around behind. The attached pronoun specifies 'his.'
6.grammar: A noun ('back') with the possessive pronoun 'his' attached at the end. The -i vowel on the noun before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word follows the preposition 'from behind' (min warāʾi) — so it reads 'his back' as the object of that phrase. The pronoun form -hi (rather than -hu) is itself pulled into the i-vowel by the preceding genitive.
6.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back, to be visible/manifest, to appear

1.meaning: Then soon / then in due course — a connective 'then' joined to a particle that points to the future, signalling that what follows is going to happen. It conveys near-certain futurity, often with a reassuring sense of 'it will surely come to pass'.
1.grammar: Fa- is a connecting particle ('then/so') that links this clause to what came before. Sawfa is a future-tense particle placed before a present-tense verb to push its meaning into the future — like English 'will' or 'shall', with a nuance of 'in time, soon'. Neither piece takes a case ending; particles are indeclinable (their form never changes).

2.meaning: He calls out / he will cry out — to raise one's voice in calling, summoning, or appealing. Here it is the doomed person crying out for his own destruction.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he calls / he will call.' The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the long -ū ending is the root's final weak letter (w). It is in the indicative (plain statement) mood. The trailing alif is a purely orthographic 'alif of separation' written after verb forms ending in -ū; it carries no sound or meaning.
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

3.meaning: Destruction / ruin / perdition — utter doom. Idiomatically one 'calls thubūr' (yadʿū thubūran), i.e. cries out 'O my destruction!' wishing for annihilation to escape the torment.
3.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the -an ending (the 'nunation,' an added -n that also marks it as indefinite: 'a destruction'). It is accusative because it is the direct object of the verb 'he calls/cries out for' — what he is calling for is destruction.
3.root: ث-ب-ر (th-b-r) — destruction, ruin, perdition

1.meaning: And he will burn / he will enter the Fire — to be scorched by and suffer a blazing fire. The verb conveys him entering and roasting in the flames.
1.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, Form I active: 'he burns / he will enter (the Fire) and suffer it.' The ya- prefix marks 'he'; the final long -ā (written with a dagger alif over yā, ٰى) is the root's weak final letter. Indicative mood. The active voweling (ya-, not passive yu-) means he himself burns/enters, not that he is 'made to roast.' The doubled w (wa-) at the start is the connecting 'and,' joined to the preceding word.
1.root: ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-y) — to roast, burn, be scorched in fire; to enter/endure a fire

2.meaning: A Blaze — a fiercely kindled, flaming fire. Saʿīr is one of the names/descriptions of the Hellfire, stressing its roaring, blazing heat.
2.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, marked by the -an ending (nunation, also signalling 'a' / indefinite). It is accusative as the object of the verb 'he will burn in / enter' (yaṣlā saʿīran) — the blaze is what he is made to enter.
2.root: س-ع-ر (s-ʿ-r) — to kindle, set ablaze; blazing fire

1.meaning: Indeed he / truly he — 'inna is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), and the attached 'he' is its subject. Together: 'Indeed he…'
1.grammar: The emphasis-particle 'inna ('indeed, truly') with the pronoun 'he' attached as its subject. 'Inna grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative, so this attached 'he' (-hu) is its accusative subject; it then awaits a predicate ('Indeed he was/used to…'). The -hu form keeps its u-vowel here because the preceding syllable has an a-vowel.

2.meaning: He was / he used to be — the past-tense verb 'to be.' With a following verb it expresses a continuous past habit ('he used to…'). Here: 'he used to be / had been.'
2.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he was.' The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he.' The long -ā in the middle is the root's hollow (weak middle) letter. Paired with a following present-tense verb it gives the sense 'he used to / would habitually,' describing ongoing past behavior.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

3.meaning: In / among — a preposition placing something inside or within a group or sphere. In context 'among his people.'
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'in, within, among.' It is an indeclinable particle (no case ending of its own) and it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case ('in/among his people'). The long -ī is simply how the word is built. Here the spelling carries a small connector (the hamza over the following word) leading into 'his people.'
3.root: — (preposition; no root)

4.meaning: His family / his people — one's household and kinfolk, the close relatives to whom one belongs. In context, the saved person returns rejoicing to his family (understood by many to include his family in Paradise).
4.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive 'his'. It is in the genitive case (-i ending on ahli-) because it follows the preposition ilā ('to'), which always governs the genitive. The attached pronoun -hi ('his') takes its i-form here because it follows that genitive i vowel. Together: 'to his family'.
4.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, household, belonging, being inhabited

5.meaning: Joyful / delighted / happy — in a state of gladness and rejoicing. It describes the person as filled with happiness as he returns to his family, the fruit of a good reckoning.
5.grammar: A passive participle ('one who has been gladdened, made joyful') in the accusative case, shown by the -an ending. It is accusative because it describes the state or condition of the subject of 'he returns' — a 'circumstantial' description telling us HOW he returns: 'he returns joyful'. This kind of state-describing word in Arabic regularly takes the accusative -an ending.
5.root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r) — joy, happiness, gladness; delight of the heart

1.meaning: Indeed he / truly he — 'inna is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), and the attached 'he' is its subject. Together: 'Indeed he…'
1.grammar: The emphasis-particle 'inna ('indeed, truly') with the pronoun 'he' attached as its subject. 'Inna grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative, so this attached 'he' (-hu) is its accusative subject; it then awaits a predicate ('Indeed he was/used to…'). The -hu form keeps its u-vowel here because the preceding syllable has an a-vowel.

2.meaning: He thought / supposed — to hold an opinion, suppose, or assume, often a conjecture short of certainty. Here it is the false assumption of the disbeliever.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he thought / supposed.' The final -a is the past-tense ending for 'he.' The doubled n (shadda) is part of the root, which has a repeated final letter. The verb introduces what he supposed in the following clause ('he supposed that he would never return').
2.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, suppose, assume, conjecture

3.meaning: That — a subordinating particle introducing a clause, here functioning as 'an' which, before a verb, often means 'that' (introducing the content of the thought/supposition).
3.grammar: A particle 'an' that introduces a following clause as the object of 'he supposed.' Here it precedes the negating word 'never' (lan) and the verb, so the whole stretch reads 'that he would never return.' It carries a sukūn (no vowel) on the n and has no case of its own.
3.root: — (particle; no root)

4.meaning: Never / will not at all — an emphatic negation of the future: it denies that something will ever happen. Stronger and future-oriented than a plain 'not.'
4.grammar: A negating particle that denies a future action: 'will never / will not at all.' It governs the following present-tense verb and forces it into the subjunctive mood (seen in the verb's -a ending). It carries a sukūn on the n. The doubled l at the start reflects its running-together with the preceding word 'an.'

5.meaning: He would return / come back — to revert or go back. In context it denotes returning (to Allah for the Resurrection and reckoning), which the disbeliever assumed would never happen.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he returns / will return.' The ya- prefix marks 'he.' The final -a is the subjunctive ending, here required by the preceding 'lan' ('never') — so it reads 'he would never return.' The long -ū in the middle is the root's hollow (weak middle) letter. Its own morphological form is yaḥūra (with a plain yāʾ); the doubled yāʾ seen in the text is a recitation (tajwīd) assimilation — the n of 'lan' merging into the following yāʾ (idghām) — not part of the verb's form.
5.root: ح-و-ر (ḥ-w-r) — to return, revert, turn back

1.meaning: An emphatic answer-particle meaning 'Yes indeed!' or 'Yes, on the contrary!' It is the specific word used to REVERSE a negative or to affirm something after a denial or a negatively-framed question. Here it overturns the disbelievers' assumption that they would never return to Allah: 'Yes, they certainly will!'

parts.en: yes indeed / on the contrary, yes

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It is the dedicated word for a positive rebuttal: it contradicts a preceding negative statement or expectation and affirms the opposite. Unlike a plain 'yes', it specifically means 'no — the truth is the reverse, and yes it WILL happen.' The two small marks following it are recitation/pause symbols, not part of the word.

2.meaning: A particle of strong emphasis placed at the head of a sentence, roughly 'Indeed…', 'Truly…', 'Surely…'. It assures the listener that what follows is certain and important. English has no exact equivalent; it lends solemn certainty to the whole statement.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle that governs the noun after it. Grammatically it puts its subject (here 'his Lord') into the accusative case, which is why the next word reads rabba-hu rather than rabbu-hu. It carries no tense or person of its own; its job is purely to stress that the coming statement is true and certain.

3.meaning: 'His Lord' — Lord here translates rabb, a rich term meaning the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs His servant. The attached 'his' refers to the human being, affirming that every person has Allah as their Lord and Caretaker.
3.grammar: Noun 'Lord' (rabb) plus the attached possessive pronoun -hu 'his'. The -a on rabba is the accusative ending, here because the word is the ism (subject) of the preceding emphatic particle inna, which puts its subject in the accusative ('indeed his Lord…'). The suffix -hu means 'his', pointing back to the person being spoken about.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain

4.meaning: He was / he used to be — the past-tense verb 'to be.' With a following verb it expresses a continuous past habit ('he used to…'). Here: 'he used to be / had been.'
4.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he was.' The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he.' The long -ā in the middle is the root's hollow (weak middle) letter. Paired with a following present-tense verb it gives the sense 'he used to / would habitually,' describing ongoing past behavior.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

5.meaning: 'Of him' / 'about him' — a small word made of the preposition bi- ('with/of/about/by') joined to the pronoun 'him'. With the attribute 'All-Seeing' (baṣīr), bi-hi conveys 'All-Seeing OF him', i.e. fully observant of the person and his deeds.
5.grammar: Preposition bi- plus the attached pronoun -hi 'him'. Any noun or pronoun after bi- takes the genitive form, which is why the pronoun appears as -hi (with an 'i' vowel) rather than -hu. It links to the word 'All-Seeing', completing the sense 'ever-Seeing of him'.

6.meaning: 'All-Seeing' — an intensive form meaning one who sees perfectly, constantly, and thoroughly. As a divine attribute it affirms that Allah perceives everything about His servant, inwardly and outwardly, missing nothing.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, permanent quality ('ever-Seeing', not just 'seeing'). The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the accusative with 'nunation', here because it is the predicate (khabar) of kāna in the verse 'his Lord has always BEEN all-seeing of him' (inna rabbahu kāna bihi baṣīran) — kāna puts its predicate in the accusative. The mark after it is a recitation/pause symbol.
6.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

1.meaning: An opening expression combining 'so/then' with an emphatic 'nay/no', often rendered 'But nay!' or 'So I do…'. Before an oath it functions as a strong attention-grabbing lead-in that heightens the solemnity of the swearing that follows.
1.grammar: A connector fa- ('so/then') joined to the negative particle lā ('no/not'). Here lā does not negate the oath itself; before swearing it is an emphatic flourish that intensifies it ('So — verily I swear!'). Both pieces are indeclinable particles with fixed endings; the elongated alif (lāʾ) is simply a recitation lengthening.

2.meaning: 'I swear' / 'I take an oath' — a first-person statement of solemn swearing, used to call a sacred witness (here the twilight) to underline the truth of what is about to be declared.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to swear' in form IV (the af'ala pattern). The opening u- prefix marks the subject 'I'; the final -u is the ordinary present-indicative ending used for a simple, ongoing statement ('I do swear'). The action is present and real, not a command or a hypothetical.
2.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to swear an oath; to divide

3.meaning: 'By the twilight glow' — refers to the reddish light on the horizon after sunset (the after-glow of dusk). Introduced by 'by', it is the object Allah swears by, a striking sign of His ordering of day and night.
3.grammar: Preposition bi- 'by' (the particle of oath) + the definite article al- 'the' + the noun shafaq 'twilight glow'. The final -i is the genitive ending, required because the word follows the preposition bi-; so it reads 'by the twilight'. (The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following sh-, hence ash-shafaq.) The mark after it is a recitation symbol.
3.root: ش-ف-ق (sh-f-q) — twilight glow; (relatedly) tenderness, apprehension

1.meaning: 'And by the night' — adds the night as a further sacred witness in the chain of oaths. 'Night' here evokes the time of darkness, rest, and the gathering-in of all that the day has scattered.
1.grammar: The particle wa- here carries a double duty: it joins this to the previous oath ('and') and itself functions as the oath-particle 'by'. With al- 'the' + layl 'night'. The final -i is the genitive ending triggered by the oath-wa, giving 'and by the night'. (The 'l' of al- merges into the following l-, hence al-layl.)

2.meaning: 'And what(ever)' — a connector 'and' joined to the relative word mā, 'that which / whatever'. Together they introduce an unspecified thing: 'and whatever it gathers up,' deliberately broad so as to include everything the night enfolds.
2.grammar: Connector wa- ('and', continuing the oath) + the relative pronoun mā ('what / whatever'). Mā is indeclinable (no case ending) and stands for an unnamed thing, here the antecedent of the verb that follows: 'and whatever [the night] envelops'. It generalizes, covering all that is gathered under the night.

3.meaning: 'It gathers up / drives together / envelops' — describes the night collecting and folding in all that was spread out during the day (creatures, light, activity), drawing them together into its darkness.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he gathered together'). It is a single indivisible word: the initial wāw is the first root letter (w-s-q), NOT a separate conjunction — the connective 'and' belongs to the preceding word wamā. The final -a is the basic past-tense ending, and the subject 'it' (the night) is built into the verb. Following mā, it completes the relative clause: 'whatever it has gathered in'. The mark after it is a recitation symbol.
3.root: و-س-ق (w-s-q) — to gather, drive together, load up

1.meaning: 'And by the moon' — adds the moon as a further witness in the series of oaths, leading into 'when it becomes full.' The moon is a sign of Allah's measured ordering of time and its phases.
1.grammar: Connective-and-oath particle wa- ('and / by') + al- 'the' + qamar 'moon'. The final -i is the genitive ending caused by the oath-wa, giving 'and by the moon'. Here the 'l' of al- is fully pronounced (al-qamar), since q- is a 'moon letter' that does not absorb the article.

2.meaning: A conditional/temporal particle meaning 'when' or 'whenever' — it sets up a circumstance and points forward to the event that will happen once that circumstance arrives. Here it introduces the great cosmic events of the Last Day.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle of time and condition, so it has no case ending that changes. It governs the verb that follows and means roughly 'at the moment when…'; it normally refers to something certain or expected to occur, unlike 'in' (if) which marks the merely hypothetical.

3.meaning: It gathers itself together into a complete whole; said of the moon, it means 'it became full, reaching its perfect roundness.' The verb conveys the idea of scattered parts being collected and harmonized into a single, evenly-balanced fullness.

parts.en: infixed -t- of Form VIII, here assimilated into the root's first letter

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he/it became full.' The final -a is simply the standard ending of this past-tense form (it carries no case meaning on verbs). This is Form VIII (the iftaʿala pattern), which often adds a sense of doing something for/to oneself, so here: the moon 'gathers its own light together' into fullness. The original w- of the root has merged into the doubled tt.
3.root: و-س-ق (w-s-q) — to gather, collect, load up, bring together

1.meaning: You will most certainly ride/mount/embark — used figuratively for moving stage by stage through successive states or conditions, as one is carried upward or onward from one phase of existence to the next.
1.grammar: A present/future verb in the 2nd person ('you'), carrying a double emphasis: the la- prefix at the front and the doubled -nna at the end together make it a solemn certainty ('you will SURELY embark'). The number is ambiguous: the surface form la-tarkabunna can be read as 2nd-person masculine singular ('you [one man] will surely ride') OR as 2nd-person masculine plural, because the plural la-tarkabūnanna contracts — the indicative -ūna loses its -na before the emphatic -nna and the -ū is absorbed, giving the same spelling. Either way, the message is addressed broadly to people/mankind. The emphatic -nna also locks the verb into a firm, future-bound mood, displacing the plain indicative ending (for a singular this replaces the bare -u; for a plural it replaces the -ūna).
1.root: ر-ك-ب (r-k-b) — to mount, ride, board, be carried upon

2.meaning: A stage, level, or layer — one condition or phase reached after another. It pictures life and the hereafter as a series of ascending tiers or states that one passes through in turn.
2.grammar: A singular indefinite noun, 'a stage.' The final -an (the 'tanwīn' fatḥa) does two jobs at once: it marks the noun as indefinite ('a stage,' not 'the stage'), and its -a vowel is the accusative/object ending, here marking it as the thing being moved onto — 'you will mount onto [a] stage.'
2.root: ط-ب-ق (ṭ-b-q) — to cover over, lie in layers; a stratum or matching level

3.meaning: A linking particle whose core sense is 'from, off of, away from, after.' Here it expresses succession — moving on 'from' one thing to reach the next, i.e. stage after stage.
3.grammar: A preposition (a small connecting word). It has no changeable ending of its own; it simply governs the noun after it, putting that noun into the genitive case. In 'ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaqin' it conveys progression: one stage 'after / off of' another.
3.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: A stage, level, or layer — the same word as id 62, here naming the stage that one moves on *from*. Together the pair means 'stage after stage,' i.e. passing through one condition after another.
4.grammar: A singular indefinite noun, 'a stage.' The final -in (the 'tanwīn' kasra) marks it as indefinite ('a stage') and, with its -i vowel, puts it in the genitive case because it follows the preposition ʿan ('from a stage'). So the -in ending is the form a noun takes after 'from.'
4.root: ط-ب-ق (ṭ-b-q) — to cover over, lie in layers; a stratum or matching level

1.meaning: 'So what...?' — an opening that introduces a reproachful, wondering question: 'So what is the matter with them...?' It expresses astonishment at people's behavior.

parts.en: so / then (connecting to what came before)

1.grammar: Two joined particles. The fa- at the front means 'so / then,' tying this sentence to the previous verses as a consequence or follow-on. The mā here is an interrogative 'what,' launching the question 'what is [the matter]...?' Neither piece changes its ending; in this idiom 'mā la-hum' literally reads 'what is to/for them?' = 'what is the matter with them?'

2.meaning: 'For them / to them' — it belongs to them, it is theirs, or it pertains to them. In the idiom 'mā lahum' it carries the sense 'what is the matter WITH them.'
2.grammar: A preposition la- ('for/to') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them,' referring to a group of males or a mixed group). Attached pronouns like this do not change for case; -hum is the fixed 'them.' The phrase answers 'to whom?' — here, paired with mā, it forms 'what is there for them / what is wrong with them.'

3.meaning: 'Not' — the basic word of negation, here denying an action: they do 'not' believe. With a present-tense verb it negates the ongoing/habitual act.
3.grammar: A negating particle placed before a present-tense verb to mean 'does not / do not.' It has no ending of its own and does not change the verb's ending; it simply turns 'they believe' into 'they do not believe.'
3.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: They believe — they have faith, putting trust and secure conviction in Allah and His message. The root also carries the ideas of safety and security, so to 'believe' is to find inward security by entrusting oneself to the truth.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural: 'they believe.' The yu- at the front plus the -ūna at the end together mean 'they (men/people) believe.' The full -ūna ending is the ordinary 'indicative' form, signalling a plain, ongoing statement; because the preceding lā simply negates it, the ending stays -ūna: 'they do not believe.' The verb is Form IV (af'ala), which here gives the settled sense 'to have faith / to grant trust.'
4.root: ء-م-ن (ʼ-m-n) — safety, security, trust; hence to believe, to feel secure in faith

1.meaning: And when — joining a second condition to the first; it introduces another event of the Last Day ('and when the earth…').
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to the indeclinable time-and-condition particle 'idhā' ('when'). 'Idhā' has no changing case ending; it governs the verb that follows and points to an event expected to occur.

2.meaning: It is recited / is read aloud — said of the Qur'an being read out to listeners. The root means to read or recite, and especially to recite Scripture.

parts.en: 1st root letter q, carrying the passive vowel u
2nd root letter r, carrying the passive vowel i

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'it was/is recited.' This is a Form I passive, built by imposing the vowel pattern u–i–a onto the three root letters q-r-ʼ (giving quri'a) — there is no separable prefix; the opening q is simply the first root letter wearing the passive's tell-tale ḍamma (u). That u-then-i shape is what signals the passive: the action is done to the subject, with no doer named, i.e. 'it is recited [to them].' The final -a is the standard past-tense ending (no case meaning on a verb). The subject that 'is recited' is al-Qur'ān, named next.
2.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʼ) — to read, recite, read aloud (the source of the word 'Qur'ān' itself)

3.meaning: 'Upon them / to them' — over or onto a group. With the verb 'recited,' it means the Qur'an is recited 'to/over them,' i.e. in their hearing.
3.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('upon/over') with the attached pronoun 'them.' Before the pronoun, ʿalā takes its joining shape ʿalay-. The pronoun is normally -him, but here it appears as -himu (with a final -u) to ease pronunciation before the next word, which begins with the joined article 'al-'. Attached pronouns do not change for case; -him(u) is the fixed 'them.' The phrase means 'recited to/over them.'
3.root: — (preposition + pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: The Qur'an — 'the Recitation,' the Book of Allah meant to be read and recited aloud. The name itself comes from the verb 'to recite,' so it means 'the thing that is recited.'
4.grammar: A definite noun: 'the Qur'an.' The al- at the front is 'the.' The final -u is the nominative ending, marking this word as the subject (the doer/topic) of its clause — here, the thing that 'is recited': '[when] the Qur'an is recited to them.' Being already definite with al-, it takes a single -u (not -un).

5.meaning: 'Not' — the basic word of negation, here denying an action: they do 'not' believe. With a present-tense verb it negates the ongoing/habitual act.
5.grammar: A negating particle placed before a present-tense verb to mean 'does not / do not.' It has no ending of its own and does not change the verb's ending; it simply turns 'they believe' into 'they do not believe.'

6.meaning: They prostrate themselves — they lower the forehead to the ground in humble worship and submission. The verb describes the ongoing or habitual act of bowing down before Allah. In context it is negated by an earlier particle ('they do NOT prostrate'). This word carries a recitation mark (sajdah symbol) indicating that a prostration is performed when reciting this verse.
6.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person ('they/he'), and the -ūna ending makes it a full masculine plural in the indicative ('they [do] prostrate'). The kept -na of -ūna shows it is in the plain indicative mood (a stated fact), not the subjunctive or jussive (which would drop it).
6.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow the face to the ground in worship

1.meaning: A particle of retraction and correction, roughly 'Nay' or 'rather / on the contrary.' It cancels or sets aside what might have been expected and redirects attention to the true state of affairs: not only do they fail to submit, but in fact they actively deny. Here it carries a connecting vowel because the next word begins with the definite article.

parts.en: helping vowel (added to ease pronunciation before the article)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case or tense). Its base form is 'bal'; the final -i here is not a grammatical case ending but a connective vowel (kasrah) supplied so the otherwise silent final letter can join smoothly onto the following 'al-' (the). Its job is to retract the previous idea and introduce a stronger, contrasting statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun introducing a group that will be described by the verb that follows ('those who disbelieved'). It points to a definite, known set of people and links them to the clause that defines them.
2.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural ('those who…'). It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it always needs a following clause (here 'disbelieved') to complete its meaning. The -īna shape signals masculine plural ('those [people] who'), as opposed to the singular alladhī ('the one who').

3.meaning: They disbelieved — they rejected faith and covered over the truth, refusing to acknowledge Allah and His message. The root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' so a disbeliever is pictured as one who buries or hides the truth he has been shown. The past-tense form states this as a completed, established fact about them.
3.grammar: Past/perfect verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they disbelieved'). The -ū ending attached to the stem means 'they' (masculine plural) and marks the action as done and completed in the past. The silent alif written after the -ū (الف الفارقة) is merely a spelling convention and is not pronounced. This verb forms the clause defining 'those who' before it.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to reject faith, to disbelieve

4.meaning: They cry lies, they deny — they persistently treat the truth (the Qur'an and the Messenger) as a falsehood and reject it. This is an intensive form (yukadhdhibūna), conveying repeated, emphatic, deliberate denial rather than a single act. The present-tense form portrays it as their ongoing, characteristic behavior.
4.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine plural, in an intensified pattern (Form II, marked by the doubled middle letter, dhdh). Assembled, the word is yukadhdhibūna with the doubled dh reflecting the shadda on the dhāl. The yu- prefix goes with this intensive/causative pattern; the -ūna ending means 'they' (masculine plural) and its kept -na marks the plain indicative mood (a stated, ongoing fact). The doubling adds force: 'they keep denying / they vehemently reject it as a lie.'
4.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call something a lie, to deny / reject as false

1.meaning: 'And Allah' — the proper name of the One True God, the sole object of worship, joined to the previous statement by 'and / but.' Here it opens a contrast: whatever they conceal, Allah knows it. The name Allah is unique and not a common noun; it cannot be made plural or feminine.
1.grammar: A connecting particle 'wa' (and/but) plus the proper name Allah. The final -u ending is nominative, which marks Allah here as the subject — the one doing the knowing ('Allah knows…'). The 'wa' joins this sentence to the previous verse and here carries a contrasting sense ('but Allah…').

2.meaning: 'Most knowing / knows best' — a superlative describing Allah's knowledge as supreme and unsurpassed. It does not merely say He knows, but that He knows more fully and perfectly than anyone, encompassing even what people hide. Functioning as the predicate, it completes 'Allah is most knowing of…'
2.grammar: A superlative/elative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('most …'), here 'most knowing.' The opening a- (hamzah) is the prefix that turns the root into a superlative, like English '-est' or 'most.' The final -u ending is nominative, fitting because it serves as the predicate describing the subject Allah ('Allah IS most knowing'). It links to what follows via 'of what…'.

3.meaning: 'Of what / about that which' — a combination of the preposition 'bi-' (here meaning 'of / about / regarding') with the word 'mā' ('what / that which'). Together they mean 'regarding that which…,' introducing the thing about which Allah is most knowing.
3.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' fused to the relative/indefinite noun 'mā' ('what, that which'). The 'bi-' attaches the following clause to 'most knowing' ('most knowing OF what…'). 'Mā' is indeclinable (it has no case ending) and here means 'that which,' pointing forward to the verb that follows ('what they conceal'). Grammatically 'mā' is in the genitive position because it follows the preposition, but its form does not visibly change.

4.meaning: They keep within / store up — they hold and conceal things inside themselves, such as hidden disbelief, secret denial, or concealed intentions. The image is of gathering something into a container and keeping it hidden away. The present tense presents this as their continual practice, all of which Allah fully knows.

parts.en: keep, store, gather and hold within

4.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they store up / keep within'). The yu- prefix marks the third person with this verb pattern, and the -ūna ending means 'they' (masculine plural) with its kept -na showing the plain indicative mood (an ongoing fact). The first root letter (w) appears as the long 'ū' sound after the prefix. The object of their concealing is what 'bimā' (the preceding word) refers to.
4.root: و-ع-ي (w-ʿ-y) — to contain, retain, keep / gather within (a vessel; also to be mindful)

1.meaning: 'So announce to them / give them tidings' — a command to the Prophet to convey news. The root means to give glad tidings, but here it is used pointedly and ironically: the 'good news' he is told to deliver is in fact a painful punishment. The 'so' draws the conclusion from their persistent denial.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in an intensified pattern (Form II, marked by the doubled middle letter, shsh), addressed to a single male ('you, announce!'). It carries no subject ending because the imperative's silent (jussive) form is its base; the suffix -hum ('them') is the object receiving the announcement. The leading fa- ('so/then') ties the command to what came before as its consequence.
1.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — glad tidings, good news (also 'skin'); to announce news

2.meaning: 'Of a punishment / with a torment' — the preposition 'bi-' ('of / with') plus 'ʿadhāb,' a severe punishment or torment. It names the content of the tidings being given ('give them tidings OF a punishment'). The word is indefinite ('a punishment'), leaving its dreadful nature open and emphasized by the adjective that follows.
2.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' plus the noun 'ʿadhāb.' The ending -in (two kasrahs, tanwīn) does two things at once: the kasrah shows the genitive case, required because the noun follows the preposition 'bi-' ('of a punishment'), and the final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment,' not 'the punishment'). It is the thing announced by the command before it.

3.meaning: 'Painful' — an adjective describing the punishment as causing intense, agonizing pain. The form is an intensive pattern, so it conveys not merely 'hurtful' but deeply, severely painful. It modifies the preceding noun 'punishment,' completing the phrase 'a painful punishment.'

parts.en: genitive + indefinite ending (-in on the final root letter m)

3.grammar: An adjective in the intensive pattern faʿīl ('painful / very painful'), describing the noun before it. The ending -in (two kasrahs, tanwīn) matches that noun exactly: the kasrah gives the genitive case (agreeing with 'punishment,' which is genitive after 'bi-'), and the final -n marks it as indefinite. Because the adjective mirrors the noun in case, definiteness, gender, and number, we read them as one phrase: 'a painful punishment.'
3.root: أ-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — pain, to be in pain; painful

1.meaning: An exceptive particle meaning 'except' or 'save'. It carves out an exception from a preceding (here implied) general statement, excluding one group from a ruling that otherwise applies. In context it sets the believers apart from the disbelievers just condemned, so that the threatened punishment does NOT apply to them.
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending or root and never changes form. Its job is to introduce the exception that follows: 'except those who...'. It signals that what comes next is being excluded from the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun introducing a group that will be described by the verb that follows ('those who disbelieved'). It points to a definite, known set of people and links them to the clause that defines them.
2.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural ('those who…'). It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it always needs a following clause (here 'disbelieved') to complete its meaning. The -īna shape signals masculine plural ('those [people] who'), as opposed to the singular alladhī ('the one who').

3.meaning: They believed / they have come to faith — to place trust and firm belief in Allah and the truth He revealed. The Form IV verb carries the sense of entering into a state of secure faith and giving one's heart's assent.

parts.en: (Form IV pattern) prefixed long 'ā' marking the 'caused to / entered into' verb pattern
stem from 'a-m-n' (to be secure, to trust)

3.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form IV (the pattern āmana, 'to believe'). The -ū ending is the subject marker meaning 'they' (a group of males, or a mixed group): 'they believed / they have believed'. The silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
3.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust

4.meaning: And they did / and they worked — to perform, carry out, and put into action. Here it points to deeds actively done, paired with faith to show that belief is completed by action.
4.grammar: 'wa' is the joining word 'and', linking this verb to the previous one. The core is a past-tense Form I verb 'ʿamila' (he did). The -ū ending is the subject marker 'they' (a group of males or mixed group): 'and they did'. So the phrase reads 'and they did [righteous deeds]'.

5.meaning: The righteous deeds — good, sound, wholesome acts that are upright and pleasing to Allah. Literally 'the things that are righteous/sound', the word functions here as the object of the verb 'they did'.

parts.en: case ending (accusative here, same form as genitive for this plural)

5.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The base is the active participle 'ṣāliḥ' (one who/that which is righteous), made feminine plural with '-āt' to mean 'righteous deeds/things'. It is the object of the verb 'they did', so it is in the accusative case. Note: for sound feminine plurals like this, the accusative and genitive share the same '-i' ending (only the nominative differs, taking '-u'); so the '-i' here marks the accusative even though it looks identical to the genitive form. Hence 'ṣāliḥāti' — 'the righteous deeds' as the thing that was done.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, righteous, upright, good

6.meaning: 'For them / to them' — it belongs to them, it is theirs, or it pertains to them. In the idiom 'mā lahum' it carries the sense 'what is the matter WITH them.'
6.grammar: A preposition la- ('for/to') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them,' referring to a group of males or a mixed group). Attached pronouns like this do not change for case; -hum is the fixed 'them.' The phrase answers 'to whom?' — here, paired with mā, it forms 'what is there for them / what is wrong with them.'

7.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the recompense due for what one has done. Here it is the never-ending reward promised to the believers for their faith and good deeds.
7.grammar: A noun, 'a reward'. The '-un' ending (the two-dots 'tanwīn' on the final letter) does two things at once: the 'u' shows it is the subject of the sentence (the thing that 'will be' for them — 'for them is a reward'), and the '-n' sound makes it indefinite, i.e. 'a reward' rather than 'the reward'.

8.meaning: Other than / without / not — literally 'other than', it negates the quality of the word that follows it. Joined with 'mamnūn' it means the reward is 'other than cut off', i.e. unending and uninterrupted.
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'other than', used here to negate the following word ('other than cut off' = 'never-ending'). The '-u' ending matches the noun it describes, 'ajrun' (the reward), agreeing with it as the subject. The word that comes after 'ghayru' is pulled into the genitive ('other than X'), which is why the next word ends in '-in'.

9.meaning: Cut off, severed, diminished, or interrupted. As a passive participle it describes something that has been broken off or made to dwindle. Negated by the preceding 'ghayru', the phrase means the reward is unfailing — never cut short and never decreasing.

parts.en: genitive ending after 'ghayru' ('...of being cut off')

9.grammar: A passive participle (the 'maf'ūl' pattern, 'mamnūn' = 'cut off / severed / diminished'). It is governed by the preceding word 'ghayru' ('other than'), which puts it in the genitive case, marked by the '-in' ending (the tanwīn of '-in'): literally 'other than [something] cut off' — that is, never-ending. The '-n' of '-in' also keeps it indefinite.
9.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to cut off / sever; also to bestow a favor
